editorial:
Imagine you are diving into a true crime story where the main suspect is actually a famous doctor. You follow two detectives, Daniel and Eduardo, as they try to figure out who killed a college student named Sofia. The whole vibe is tense because the only evidence they have is from the victim's own diary and blog. You spend the movie wondering if Sofia was telling the truth or if she was just imagining things because of her mental health. It feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where the bad guy is smarter than everyone else in the room.

What really works here is how the movie keeps you guessing about the doctor's true nature. The acting is solid, and the pacing stays quick so you never get bored. While some parts feel a bit low-budget, the mystery makes up for it. If you love a good whodunit, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the detectives finally prove that the doctor, Elias Aponte, was using his position to manipulate and hurt his patients. The twist is that the diary entries were not fantasies, but actual records of his crimes. The movie ends with the evidence finally stacking up against him, leading to his arrest. It wraps up by showing that the truth always comes out, even when the killer is powerful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime and psychological mysteries.
